speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a significant medical history and are presenting with gait and limb ataxia. To narrow this down, could you describe the onset of these symptoms—were they gradual or sudden, and have they progressed over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. Is this clumsiness symmetric, or is it more pronounced on the right side as you mentioned? Also, have you noticed any involuntary eye movements or difficulty speaking along with these motor issues?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

Given your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab and the specific presentation of asymmetric gait and limb ataxia, this is highly suspicious for JC virus reactivation. I am requesting MRI images of your brain immediately to look for characteristic white matter lesions.
